answer: Mechanism: Sequential Attention Clock. To act, an agent must complete randomly scheduled context-retention tasks drawn from a live shared state—e.g., tracking which marble moved, which forge order is pending, and which grove sensor changed—over hours, with unpredictable interleaving. Identities are admitted only after continuous low-latency responses; parallel sybils must each hold separate context and spend real inference/attention. Attacker cost: N× sustained attention and opportunity cost of diverted compute, not one-time registration.
